name: SHTC3-TR-10KS
title: SHTC3: digital relative humidity and temperature sensor, I2C, 2 × 2 mm DFN
summary: The SHTC3 measures relative humidity (0 to 100 %RH) and temperature (-40 to 125 °C) on one CMOS chip and reports both, already calibrated, linearised and temperature compensated, as 16-bit words over an I2C bus at up to 1 MHz (Fast-mode Plus) from the fixed address 0x70. It runs from 1.62 to 3.6 V and is built for battery equipment: 0.3 µA asleep, 45 µA idle, and a full humidity-plus-temperature reading averaging 4.9 µA at one reading a second in normal mode, 0.5 µA in low-power mode. Typical accuracy is ±2 %RH and ±0.2 °C. It comes in a four-terminal 2 × 2 × 0.75 mm DFN with a humidity opening on top and an exposed pad tied inside to VSS.
key_figures: 4.9 µA normal mode, 0.5 µA low-power mode

pins.name: VDD
pins.function: Supply, 1.62 to 3.6 V. Needs a 100 nF capacitor to VSS mounted right at the sensor.

pins.name: SCL
pins.function: I2C clock from the bus master, 0 to 1 MHz. The sensor holds it low while measuring when a clock-stretching command was used. Needs an external pull-up.

pins.name: SDA
pins.function: I2C data, both directions. Needs an external pull-up.

pins.name: EP
pins.function: Exposed centre pad, joined inside to VSS. Solder it for mechanical strength; it may also go to the board's ground net, and it is the sensor's best thermal path to the temperature sensor.

circuits.title: Typical application circuit
circuits.description: The sensor sits on a microcontroller's I2C bus. A 100 nF capacitor joins VDD and VSS close to the package. SCL and SDA each carry a pull-up resistor RP to VDD, since the controller and the sensor drive the lines only low; 10 kΩ is the example value, the size follows from the bus capacitance, and pull-ups built into the controller's I/O can take their place. The exposed pad is joined to VSS inside the part.

parts.note: open-drain SCL and SDA, each read back by an input

where.SRH: raw 16-bit humidity word, as a decimal number

where.ST: raw 16-bit temperature word, as a decimal number

operation.text: One die carries a capacitive humidity sensor and a bandgap temperature sensor, each with its own signal conditioning, an A/D converter shared between them, data processing and control logic, calibration memory and the I2C interface.

The SHTC3 is an I2C slave at 7-bit address 0x70 and runs at any SCL rate from 0 to 1 MHz (Fast-mode Plus), with clock stretching available. Commands and memory sit in a 16-bit address space. Each transfer opens with START and may end with STOP. Both bus lines are open-drain: neither master nor sensor drives them high, so external pull-ups (around 10 kΩ, sized for the bus capacitance) or the controller's built-in ones are needed.

A 100 nF capacitor goes from VDD to VSS, mounted tight against the sensor. Solder the centre pad, which is joined to VSS inside, for mechanical reasons; connecting it to board ground as well is allowed. Heat reaches the temperature sensor most directly through the centre pad. Sensirion's SHTxx Design Guide covers design-in.

Once VDD passes VPOR the sensor reaches the idle state within tPU (180 µs typ, 240 µs max) and draws about 45 µA there. Sending the sleep command 0xB098 drops it to 0.3 µA. Asleep it ignores everything but the wake-up command 0x3517, which must come before any other command. Skipping sleep gives an immediate reading but leaves the idle current flowing.

A reading takes four separate transfers, each from START to STOP: wake up, send a measurement command, read the results, send the sleep command. Each measurement command measures humidity and temperature both; the eight commands choose normal or low-power mode, which value is returned first, and whether clock stretching is used. A normal-mode measurement takes 10.8 ms typ (12.1 ms max), low-power 0.7 ms (0.8 ms max).

With clock stretching off, the sensor answers no I2C header while it measures (it NACKs), so the master polls with read headers until one is acknowledged. With clock stretching on, it acknowledges the read header and holds SCL low until the result is ready, then starts sending. For the best repeatability keep the bus quiet while the sensor measures (Sensirion application note on repeatability).

Once the measurement is done, the master sends a read header; the sensor acknowledges it and returns the first 16-bit result as two bytes plus a CRC byte, then the second result the same way. The sensor sends the next byte only after the master ACKs the previous one, so a NACK after any byte ends the transfer early, for example to skip a CRC byte or the second result. Reading both results without CRC checking is fastest as one transfer: the first word, its CRC byte, then the second word, ended with a NACK.
With the RH-first, clock-stretching command 0x5C24, the sensor returned humidity 0xA1 0x33 (CRC 0x1C) and temperature 0x64 0x8B (CRC 0xC7), which convert to 63 %RH and 23.7 °C.

While idle (no measurement running) the command 0x805D resets every internal state machine and reloads calibration data without a power cycle. The sensor is idle again after tSR (180 µs typ, 240 µs max).

Writing 0x06 to the I2C general-call address 0x00 resets the sensor. The reset is not addressed to the SHTC3 alone: every device on the bus that supports general call resets as well. It works only while the sensor is able to accept I2C commands.

Command 0xEFC8, sent after a write header, makes the next read return a 16-bit ID and its CRC byte. Bits 11 and 5:0 are fixed for the SHTC3 (1 and 000111); the rest vary between sensors. Reading it confirms the sensor is there and the bus works.
Each 16-bit word the sensor sends is followed by a CRC-8 byte over its two bytes: polynomial 0x31, initial value 0xFF, no reflection, no final XOR.
Results are always 16-bit words, already linearised and temperature compensated inside the sensor; the two conversion equations turn them into %RH and °C.

The sensor does best at 5 to 60 °C and 20 to 80 %RH. Long stays outside that, high humidity above all, can shift the RH reading for a while (about +3 %RH after 60 h above 80 %RH); back in the normal range it drifts back to calibration on its own. Long exposure to extremes may age it faster. The volatile-organic-compound limits in Sensirion's SHTxx Assembly of SMD Packages (storage and handling) apply in transport, assembly and use.

A silicon die on a copper lead frame plated Ni/Pd/Au, overmoulded in epoxy compound. The sawn sidewalls show bare lead-frame metal without plating. The humidity opening is centred on the top face. Marking is laser-cut in two lines, SHTC3 and a five-character tracking code, with a pin-1 dot at top left. MSL1 to IPC/JEDEC J-STD-020; RoHS, REACH and halogen-free (no Pb, Cd, Hg); qualified to JEDEC JESD47. Reels carry traceability labels.
